skill.name: seo-authority-builder
skill.description: Analyzes content for experience, expertise, authority, and trust signals, then recommends concrete credibility improvements, especially for sensitive YMYL topics.
skill.summary: Builds practical E-E-A-T enhancement plans for stronger content credibility and topical authority.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All three static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown text, not executable commands or network reconnaissance. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or other semantic security issue was found.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 30 uses backticks only to format a relative documentation path in Markdown. It contains no Ruby, shell command, or execution instruction.
Lines 89-99 are a fenced Markdown example of the expected E-E-A-T report format. The block contains plain text and no executable shell or Ruby syntax.
Lines 123-124 list fact-checking and correction policies as trust signals. They contain no host discovery, scanning command, network target, or reconnaissance workflow.

content.value_statement: Content can lack visible evidence of expertise, authority, and trust. This skill audits those signals and creates a prioritized improvement plan.
actual_capabilities: Reviews content for experience, expertise, authority, and trust signals.
Identifies missing author credentials, citations, policies, and social proof.
Creates a prioritized E-E-A-T enhancement plan with current and target scores.
Suggests topical authority tactics, internal linking improvements, and content coverage areas.
Recommends author profiles, editorial policies, trust elements, and appropriate schema types.
Produces scorecards, checklists, authority maps, citation strategies, and implementation guidance.
limitations: It does not verify credentials, testimonials, certifications, or factual claims independently.
Its E-E-A-T scores are advisory assessments, not official Google metrics.
It cannot guarantee rankings, traffic growth, knowledge panels, or search visibility.
Legal, medical, and financial content still requires qualified expert review.

use_cases.title: Audit YMYL Articles
use_cases.description: Find missing expertise, sourcing, authorship, and trust signals before publishing sensitive content.

use_cases.title: Strengthen Brand Authority
use_cases.description: Plan author pages, original research, partnerships, media proof, and organizational transparency.

use_cases.title: Improve Site Trust
use_cases.description: Review policies, contact access, team biographies, reviews, and structured data across a website.

prompt_templates.title: Quick E-E-A-T Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this content for E-E-A-T signals. List the strongest signals, the main gaps, and three priority improvements: [content]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a first review of one page or article.

prompt_templates.title: Author Credibility Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this author biography for credentials, experience, transparency, and topic relevance. Suggest only claims that can be supported: [biography]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when improving author pages or bylines.

prompt_templates.title: YMYL Trust Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an E-E-A-T enhancement plan for this YMYL page. Cover expert review, citations, policies, updates, corrections, and schema: [page content]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before publishing health, finance, safety, or legal information.

prompt_templates.title: Topical Authority Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these pages as a topic cluster: [page list]. Map coverage gaps, internal links, evidence needs, expert contributions, and measurable priorities.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a multi-page authority strategy.

output_examples.input: Review a nutrition article with an anonymous author, two unsourced claims, and no update date.
output: Current assessment: weak authorship and sourcing signals.
Priority one: add a qualified author and medical reviewer biography.
Priority two: cite primary sources beside health claims.
Priority three: show publication, review, and update dates.

output_examples.input: Improve authority for a small cybersecurity consultancy website.
output: Publish team profiles with relevant certifications and project experience.
Add evidence-based case studies with approved client details.
Document editorial, disclosure, privacy, and correction policies.
Connect service pages to original research and technical guidance.

output_examples.input: Plan topical authority for a home energy efficiency website.
output_examples.output: Create clusters for insulation, heating, ventilation, audits, and incentives. Link each guide to expert profiles, standards, sources, and related case studies.

best_practices: Provide the page content, audience, topic, author details, and available evidence.
Validate every recommended credential, review, citation, testimonial, and certification before publication.
Prioritize changes by user risk, evidence quality, implementation effort, and page importance.
anti_patterns: Do not invent credentials, reviews, research, partnerships, awards, or expert approval.
Do not treat an advisory E-E-A-T score as a Google ranking metric.
Do not add trust badges or schema that misrepresent the organization or content.

faq.question: What content does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes articles, landing pages, author biographies, policy pages, topic clusters, and other content supplied in the prompt.

faq.question: Does this skill provide an official Google E-E-A-T score?
faq.answer: No. Any score is an advisory framework for prioritizing improvements, not an official Google metric.

faq.question: Can it guarantee higher search rankings?
faq.answer: No. It recommends credibility and authority improvements, but rankings depend on many technical, competitive, and content factors.

faq.question: Is it suitable for YMYL content?
faq.answer: Yes, but qualified professionals must verify sensitive medical, financial, legal, and safety information before publication.

faq.question: Can it create author biographies?
faq.answer: It can propose a biography structure and wording from supplied facts. Users must verify every credential and experience claim.

faq.question: Does it implement schema markup?
faq.answer: It recommends suitable schema types and implementation considerations. The final markup requires platform-specific validation and testing.
